title: Environmental Psychology
summary: Environmental psychology: environmental stress, crowding, noise, sustainability, person-environment interaction, proxemics, territoriality, and built environment.
revision: Environmental psychology: environmental stressors, crowding, noise, sustainability, person-environment interaction, proxemics.
traps: Stressors: noise, crowding, pollution, urban stress.

notes.t: The study of transactions between individuals and their physical settings, including how environments affect behavior and well-being.

i: Noise: unwanted sound affecting concentration and stress
Crowding: perceived density and lack of personal space
Pollution: air, water, noise affecting health
Environmental preference: natural vs built settings

notes.t: Sustainability and pro-environmental behavior involve actions that protect the environment, encouraged through awareness, incentives, and design.
UGC NET may ask about environmental stressors, proxemics, and person-environment interaction.

mnemonics.title: CPST
mnemonics.text: C — Crowding (density stress), P — Proxemics (personal space), S — Sustainability (eco-behavior), T — Territoriality (space defense)

flashcards.a: Transactions between individuals and physical settings.
